title: Habitability and Signs of Life
description: A planet's warmth comes first from its star: how bright, how near, how much light the planet reflects. Its air can be read when it passes in front of the star: starlight through the thin ring of atmosphere picks up the gases' lines, a change of a few parts in a million. Oxygen and methane together would be a sign of life, since each destroys the other and something must keep making both. Adds transit spectroscopy to the Reflecting Telescope.

puzzle.goal: A planet at distance a from a star of temperature T★ and radius R★ reflects a fraction A of the light. Balancing what it absorbs against what it radiates, write its equilibrium temperature T.
puzzle.name: Equilibrium temperature
puzzle.ask: Find T in kelvin for the Sun (Ts = 5772 K, Rs = 6.96e8 m), a = @{a} m and A = 0.3.
puzzle.method: Absorbed: σTs⁴·(Rs/a)²·πR²·(1 − A). Radiated: 4πR²·σT⁴. Solve for T.
